items.title: John L. Jones Interview, 1972-06-05
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Buddy Caieri or something like that... [INTERVIEWEE] Maybe he did. It was before my time.

ctx.x: Joe Walker was a rudiment drummer. Clyde know what I'm talking about. He mostly played, he played everything by music, rudiments. Everything was rudiments. But Boleg was a man that, he used to go in the picture show and those days they didn't have no sound pictures and he'd catch everything that'd go on. He had everything on the drums, all kinds of things. See, like a man be, you know, somebody be whistling on the television, he'd whistle. In the movie? Yeah, crickets. Yeah. Yeah, he'd catch that. He used to have…

Well, let's see now. Some of the other guys. Buddy Caieri or something like that. I never have known how you pronounce that name. Who? I've seen this written down. K-Y-E-R-I. Buddy Caieri? I don't even know what he played, but he's supposed to play with Clayman Williams.

Maybe he did. It was before my time. Yeah. Well, who did you know in that band? Lawrence Hall was a trumpet player. You got him? I heard the name. He was from the Poemville, but he came up all the time to sit in. And then we had, oh, another, Willie Daly. He died right here. But he didn't play anymore. You ever heard of him? No, I can't remember.
